name: Daoine sídhe

attributes.name: barrow
attributes.attribute: ancient mound home of the fairies
Recorded in the spellings daoine si and sidh, with Deena Shee as the English phonetic form
Serves as a polite name in Modern Irish and in Scottish Gaelic speech
Mound link read as a sign that the fairy folk descend from them

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Daoine sídhe is an Irish term for fairy folk. The name means folk from the mound. MacKillop records the older spellings daoine si and sidh. Reformed Irish now spells the term daoine si. English speech renders the name as Deena Shee. These figures were once deities. The Tuatha Dé Danann dwindled into folktale figures. MacKillop reads the mound link as a sign that the fairy folk descend from the Tuatha Dé Danann. They came to live in ancient barrows. They also lived in hillforts. They used other prehistoric monuments of Ireland. People used many flattering names to win their good will. The fairies could be amoral and mischievous. People called them The Good Folk, daoine maithe. People called them The Gentry, daoine uaisle. The first name means good people and the second noble people. Some simply called them Them. MacKillop places these polite names in Modern Irish speech and in Scottish Gaelic speech alike. The mound was their traditional home.

okr.objective: This record documents Daoine sídhe, the Irish polite name for fairy folk, folk from the mound.
key_results: Daoine sídhe means folk from the mound and euphemizes the fairies.
MacKillop records the spellings daoine si and sidh plus the English form Deena Shee.
The mound link points to descent from the Tuatha Dé Danann.
The name serves Modern Irish and Scottish Gaelic speech alike.
Flattering names such as daoine maithe and daoine uaisle won fairy good will.
